formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the spender's allowance over the owner's USDC to exactly `value`. It replaces any earlier allowance and does not add to it.
Uses up the owner's current permit nonce, so an older signature with the same nonce can no longer be used.
The signature works until `deadline`. A deadline of type(uint256).max means it never expires.
Signing moves no tokens by itself. The spender can later move up to `value` USDC from the owner.
formats.shown: The screen says "Authorize spending of tokens" and shows the spender address in raw form, the maximum amount in USDC ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit has one test, a 250 USDC amount, so the "Unlimited" threshold path is never tested.
findings.evidence: Descriptor, field `value`: "threshold": "0x8000…", "message": "Unlimited". cases/0.json has only value "250000000", which renders as "250 USDC".
findings.fix: Add a test case with value = type(uint256).max and check that the screen shows "Max spending amount: Unlimited".

findings.title: Permit shows the deadline as a date, but the code reads uint256 max as "no expiration".
findings.evidence: EIP2612.sol _permit: require(deadline == type(uint256).max || deadline >= now, ...). Descriptor, field `deadline`: format "date", encoding "timestamp", with no special-value message.
findings.fix: If the wallet supports it, show a message such as "No expiry" when the deadline is type(uint256).max.
